model.note: Stylised, normalised version of the Proof of Sampling deterrence condition. Costs are in units of one honest computation/verification, C = 1. The solver's reward R and slashable bond S are multiples of C. The minimum sampling rate that makes honesty the dominant strategy is p* = C / [(1 - r)*S + (1 - 2r)*R] (Proposition 1). EV(cheat)(p) = R - p*D and EV(honest) = R - C, with D = (1 - r)*S + (1 - 2r)*R, so the two cross exactly at p*.

presets.label: spML (r=10%)
presets.note: The paper's spML construction: reward R = 1.2C, slashable bond S = 150C, 10% Byzantine validators, full slash paid to the catcher. p* lands at ~0.736% — the stated overhead.

presets.label: opML (no bounty)
presets.note: Optimistic ML with the same bond but no catch payout: a rational verifier won't pay C to look, sampling decays toward zero, and ~0.98% of fraud settles undetected.

presets.label: Thin bond
presets.note: A lazy network: small bond, fat reward, a third of validators colluding. The deterrence threshold balloons past 10% — you have to sample almost everything to stay honest.

source.label: Zhang et al., Proof of Sampling (arXiv:2405.00295)
